newsitem.title: JAPAN: S&P revises down Daiwa Sec, Nikko Sec debt outlook.
newsitem.headline: S&P revises down Daiwa Sec, Nikko Sec debt outlook.

text.p: Standard & Poor's Corp (S&P) said on Wednesday it had revised the long-term debt outlook for Daiwa Securities Co Ltd and Nikko Securities Co Ltd to negative from stable.
The revision also applies to the long-term debt of the brokerage firms' respective affiliates, S&P said.
S&P also said it had affirmed the long- and short-term ratings of Daiwa and Nikko and their affiliates.

S&P affirmed Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd's long-term debt rating at BBB+ and its outlook at negative. The AA-/A-1+ ratings of Nomura Securities Co Ltd and its affiliates remain on CreditWatch with negative implications.
S&P said it was concerned that the capital of Daiwa, Nikko and Yamaichi may slightly diminish as a result of the possible disposal of problem loans at their finance company affiliates.
Although none of the firms have announced such plans, S&P said that Nomura has disclosed that it provided financial assistance to a troubled affiliate, which has implications for the firm.

For Daiwa, Nikko and Yamaichi, it said the expected drop in their capital is now deemed insufficient to warrant further rating action given the affiliates' minor role within their parent organisations and the parent firms' current rating levels.

S&P said that the revised outlook for Nikko and Daiwa also reflects its lingering concern over the competitive environment for brokerage firms in Japan, and the effect this may have on their risk profiles over time.
